The efficacy and safety of Lumizyme 2000 L were studied in a multicenter randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that enrolled patients with late-onset Pompe disease.

design.text: Multicenter randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 2:1 to 20 mg/kg alglucosidase alfa IV every two weeks or placebo for 78 weeks.

citations.quote: The efficacy and safety of Lumizyme 2000 L were studied in a multicenter randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial that enrolled patients with late-onset Pompe disease.

Patients were randomized 2:1, using a computerized minimization algorithm for randomization rather than blocked randomization, to either 20 mg/kg of the 2000L product administered intravenously every two weeks or placebo. Ninety patients were studied.
Patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio and received LUMIZYME or placebo every other week for 78 weeks (18 months).

population.text: Patients 8 years and older with late-onset Pompe disease, naïve to enzyme replacement therapy, ambulatory, not requiring invasive ventilatory support, with FVC between 30 and 79% of predicted.

citations.quote: Enrollment in the trial, Late-Onset Treatment Study or LOTS, was restricted to patients 8 years and older who were naïve to enzyme replacement therapy, ambulatory, did not require invasive ventilatory support, and had an FVC between 30 and 79% of the predicted normal value in a healthy population.

endpoint.text: Co-primary endpoints: distance walked during the six-minute walk test (6MWT) and upright percent predicted forced vital capacity (FVC); the statistical plan stated the 6MWT was to be examined first and FVC evaluated only if the 6MWT effect was statistically significant.

citations.quote: The original design was a 52-week trial with co-primary endpoints: 1) distance walked during the six minute walk test (6MWT) at 52 weeks, adjusted for the baseline, and 2) upright percent of predicted forced vital capacity (FVC) at 52 weeks, adjusted for the baseline.
The statistical plan stated that the 6MWT was to be examined first and if the effect was statistically significant, the percentage of predicted FVC could be evaluated.
Ninety patients were studied.
The study population included 34 males and 26 females (N=60) in the LUMIZYME group and 11 males and 19 females (N=30) in the placebo group.

indication.text: LUMIZYME (alglucosidase alfa) is a lysosomal glycogen-specific enzyme indicated for patients 8 years and older with late (non-infantile) onset Pompe disease (GAA deficiency) who do not have evidence of cardiac hypertrophy.

citations.quote: LUMIZYME (alglucosidase alfa) is a lysosomal glycogen-specific enzyme indicated for patients 8 years and older with late (non-infantile) onset Pompe disease (GAA deficiency) who do not have evidence of cardiac hypertrophy.

target_moa.text: Alglucosidase alfa is a recombinant human acid α-glucosidase (GAA) that replaces deficient lysosomal enzyme; after IV administration it is internalized via cell membrane mannose-6-phosphate receptors and taken up by lysosomes, where it degrades glycogen by catalyzing the hydrolysis of its glycosidic linkages in Pompe disease.

citations.quote: Alglucosidase alfa is a purified analog of naturally occurring, endogenous lysosomal GAA, produced by recombinant DNA technology developed in a Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cell line.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were infusion reactions including anaphylaxis, urticaria, diarrhea, vomiting, dyspnea, pruritus, rash/erythema. Serious reactions included anaphylaxis; two LUMIZYME-treated patients discontinued due to anaphylactic reactions. Based on exposure of 90 patients.

citations.quote: The most frequently reported adverse reactions (≥5%) in clinical studies were infusion reactions and included: anaphylaxis, urticaria, diarrhea, vomiting, dyspnea, pruritus, rash/erythema, pharyngolaryngeal pain, neck pain, hypoxosis, flushing/feeling hot, pain in extremity, fall and chest discomfort (6.1).

Assessment of adverse reactions is based on the exposure of 90 patients (45 male, 45 female) with late-onset Pompe disease, ages 10 to 70 years, to 20 mg/kg LUMIZYME or placebo in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled s
Two patients receiving LUMIZYME discontinued the study due to anaphylactic reactions.

detail.text: Life-threatening anaphylactic reactions, severe allergic reactions and immune mediated reactions have been observed during LUMIZYME infusions; appropriate medical support should be available. Because of the potential risk of rapid disease progression in Pompe disease patients less than 8 years of age, LUMIZYME is available only through a restricted distribution program (LUMIZYME ACE Program).

citations.quote: Life-threatening anaphylactic reactions, severe allergic reactions and immune mediated reactions have been observed in some patients during LUMIZYME™ infusions. Therefore, appropriate medical support should be readily available when LUMIZYME is administered [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1, 5.2)].

Because of the potential risk of rapid disease progression in Pompe disease patients less than 8 years of age, LUMIZYME is available only through a restricted distribution program called the LUMIZYME ACE ProgramSM.

summary.text: The original BLA for Lumizyme 2000 L (submitted May 30, 2008) was granted priority review and taken to the EMDAC on October 21, 2008, where the committee voted 16-1 that effectiveness was demonstrated and recommended accelerated approval based on FVC. After multiple Complete Response actions (first CR dated February 27, 2009) for manufacturing/CMC deficiencies, FDA and the applicant agreed that Pompe Registry outcomes data could support regular (not accelerated) approval. Alglucosidase alfa carries orphan drug designation (1997). The product was approved May 24, 2010 with a Boxed Warning and a REMS.
